question: Is the reported gain from context-augmented supervision in arxiv:2609.12230 attributable to passage coherence, or is it a context-volume / question-distribution effect that a token-matched random-distractor control would absorb?
description: arxiv:2609.12230 matches the base model, LoRA setup, optimizer, sequence length, batch size, epochs and learning-rate schedule across the KG-grounded and CG-grounded arms and uses equal QA-item counts, but each CG item contains additional supporting triples, so the context-augmented arm consumes more context tokens per example. No random-distractor or unrelated-entity-neighbourhood arm (the arxiv:2609.10237 design) was run, so the reported +1.5 to +3.8 point gains at 3/4/5-hop cannot yet be attributed to passage coherence rather than to more context tokens, a different question distribution, or the added reasoning traces that come with CG-grounded items.
confidence_basis: Based on an inference-time 1-hop threshold sweep in the appendix of arxiv:2609.12230; relevant but not the training-time matched-token control the question asks for.
rationale: This is the difference between 'context coherence is the active ingredient' and 'more grounded tokens help', which is the only remaining scientific question the pipeline poses; it is also cheap to test as an ablation on the existing setup.
resolution: Partial evidence against a pure context-volume explanation has appeared, but attribution is still not established. The appendix threshold sweep in arxiv:2609.12230 shows 1-hop accuracy that is non-monotone in the mean number of context triples per row (accuracy rises then falls as the similarity threshold loosens), which is hard to explain if more context tokens simply help. However, that sweep is inference-time on 1-hop questions with the frozen base model, and it changes relevance and volume together, so it does not separate passage coherence from token count for the training-time comparison. No random-distractor or unrelated-entity arm exists in the published work, and the only matched-context swap in the literature remains the inference-time control of arxiv:2609.10237. A training-time, token-matched arm is still required before the +1.5 to +3.8 point gains can be attributed.
